name: exposure-slider
title: Exposure Slider
description: A camera-style exposure control: a horizontal ruler of fine ticks you drag to change exposure, with a small circular gauge and number above it. The demo photo brightens or darkens as the value moves.
use: A photo editor or camera UI needs a precise exposure dial with a ruler and a numeric readout.
avoid: It is a horizontal drag-only control with no keyboard path, so a standard range input is more accessible.
a11y: The ruler is a pointer-only div with no slider role, value text or keyboard handling, though the spring is skipped under reduced motion. (keyboard: no, labels: none, reduced motion: respected)
looks: Below a dawn mountain photo sits a small dark control: a thin circular ring with a number in the middle, above a horizontal ruler of evenly spaced hairline ticks that fade toward the edges. The centre tick glows amber; positive values brighten the photo and negative values dim it.
behaves: Dragging the ruler slides the ticks under a fixed centre mark; the ring fills an amber arc from the top and the number springs to the nearest step. Releasing snaps to the nearest tick, and the value also drives the demo photo's brightness.
customise: Min, max, step, default value, accent colour, indicator visibility and an onChange callback are props; the ruler width and spring are constants.
weight: light: A ruler of tick divs and one SVG ring driven by motion values.
